cases.text: The aqueduct was an abacus. Each sluice measured a separate flow, and together the measurements showed the valley's water.
The brazier was a blanket and a nettle. It comforted every visitor and stung every visitor.
The granary was a clasp and a colander: before harvest it kept every kernel; during famine it portioned rations.
The orrery was a sextant and an eyelid: its lens angled north for a meteor, then shuttered against glare.
The cistern was a diadem and a manacle. It governed the courtyard and restrained the courtyard.
The windmill was a scythe and a bolster. It severed the air and cushioned the air.
